nodes.label: Exact-one-reference-led multi-site quota rationale
nodes.rationale: For multi-site assignments, one strongly matched live reference grounds one version in external evidence while leaving the remaining versions free to derive coherent, independent directions from project truth and Brain rules.

nodes.label: Single-site no-random-reference rationale
nodes.rationale: A single website should not be forced around an automatically selected external page because an arbitrary template can displace the project’s actual offer, evidence, audience needs, and best structure; a user-supplied reference remains allowed.

nodes.label: Documented no-fit exception rationale
nodes.rationale: Reference fit matters more than satisfying a quota mechanically, so a documented search that finds no strong match permits all versions to remain original designs instead of forcing a random or misleading model.

nodes.label: No cross-inheritance rationale
nodes.rationale: Reference-specific grid, opening composition, section dramaturgy, typography, surfaces, and motion stay in the named reference-led version so the other versions remain genuinely independent; only shared facts, user questions, and the objectively best broad structure may recur.

nodes.label: Open Adaptation Depth

nodes.label: Exact-one reference-led multi-site quota
nodes.rationale: A single strong reference gives one multi-site version concrete external evidence while preserving the independence of the remaining versions; zero is allowed only after a documented no-fit search.

nodes.label: Landing-page usefulness before style intensity
nodes.rationale: Users must understand the offer, encounter a concrete content anchor, and see the next action before expressive styling can add value.

nodes.label: Mobile comprehension as information-density measure
nodes.rationale: A narrow viewport exposes excess information most clearly, so mobile comprehension is the controlling measure for content density.

nodes.label: Mobile second-viewport progression
nodes.rationale: The second mobile viewport must begin a new user question or proof so scrolling advances understanding instead of prolonging the same hero statement.

nodes.label: Semantic-H1 readability
nodes.rationale: The sole semantic page title must remain fully readable across narrow widths, zoom, large text, masks, and sticky headers because decorative cropping must never remove meaning.

nodes.label: Content anchors over empty hero gestures
nodes.rationale: Scale, retro styling, and whitespace cannot establish relevance by themselves; a hero needs a concrete offer, object, proof, or useful mechanism.
nodes.norm_label: content anchors over empty hero gestures

nodes.label: Landing-page usefulness before style intensity
nodes.rationale: Landing-page expression is valuable only after the offer, concrete anchor, and next action form a coherent and immediately useful composition.

nodes.label: Semantic-H1 readability
nodes.rationale: The semantic H1 carries the page identity and therefore cannot be clipped, masked, overlapped, or hidden at any required viewport or zoom level.

nodes.label: Mobile second-viewport progression
nodes.rationale: A landing page must reveal the next real question or first proof within the second mobile viewport to maintain informational progress.

nodes.label: Image-optional content anchors
nodes.rationale: A real interface, calculator, process, document, case, or typographic proof can anchor a hero as effectively as an image, so imagery is optional while concrete evidence is not.

nodes.label: Limited retro systems
nodes.rationale: A full epoch simulation can overpower the actual brand and reduce trust or readability, so it requires explicit user intent or essential brand evidence.

nodes.label: Shared useful multi-site structure
nodes.rationale: Variants may reuse the objectively strongest information architecture and user-question sequence because differentiation belongs in coherent art direction, not degraded utility.

nodes.label: Exact-one reference-led multi-site quota with documented no-fit exception
nodes.rationale: Exactly one strongly matched reference should shape exactly one multi-site version, preventing both arbitrary reference multiplication and covert cross-version inheritance; no reference requires a documented no-fit result.
nodes.norm_label: exact-one reference-led multi-site quota with documented no-fit exception

nodes.label: Limited retro systems
nodes.rationale: Historical typography may support a bounded role, but a site-wide period system needs explicit intent or brand necessity because style distance alone does not justify it.

nodes.label: Semantic-H1 readability
nodes.rationale: Responsive type scaling, wrapping, and layout must preserve the complete semantic title because the only readable H1 cannot be treated as decorative material.

nodes.label: Landing-page usefulness rationale
nodes.rationale: A landing page earns expression by connecting a clear offer, a concrete proof or subject, a readable next action, and the next user question; visual intensity, oversized type, retro styling, or empty space cannot substitute for that useful content anchor.

nodes.label: Propagation and change-log governance rationale
nodes.rationale: Canonical changes can affect workflows, templates, project artifacts, tests, operations, and QA simultaneously; trigger-based propagation plus a Change Log record prevents partial updates and makes verification and remaining review obligations auditable.
